subject: Data sovereignty playbook — post-call summary & MAP
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Morgan <taylor.morgan@avahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Data sovereignty playbook — post-call summary & MAP

Hi Taylor — thanks again for the time today. Short recap from our side with the concrete asks we heard and proposed next steps. I’ve attached a short playbook and a worksheet that captures the network constraints you shared.

Key business drivers (your words):
- Regulatory requirement: state-level data residency for PHI and derived model outputs.
- Procurement mandate: no cross-border egress of raw data; logs/evidence must stay within the US region.
- Security posture: preference for a private control plane and HSM-backed key management; SOC 2 + HITRUST are high priority.

Technical constraints you flagged:
- Primary inference must run in a VPC in us-east-2; no public-facing endpoints in the compute plane.
- Egress allowed only via a customer-managed NAT for telemetry; all outbound destinations must be explicitly whitelisted.
- Requirement for an air-gapped option for a narrow workload (batch PHI redaction) with periodic physical media transfer for audit archives.
- Minimum latency SLO for UI call-path: 120ms p95 for short prompts (50–120 tokens) — this is a hard constraint for your triage flow.

Immediate asks / proposed MAP (owners + ETA):
1) Redwood provides a high-level deployment design and ACL list for your infra team (Jonas) — deliver by 2027-08-12.
2) Security to kickoff a short KMS/HSM compatibility note and required certs list (Ben) — deliver by 2027-08-13.
3) Work with Ava infra to enumerate NAT/whitelist endpoints and firewall rules in the attached spreadsheet (Taylor / Ava infra) — target 2027-08-16.
4) Draft a scoped air-gap operating procedure for redaction batch runs (Marissa + Ava security) — draft by 2027-08-20.

Open questions we need clarity on from your side:
- For the air-gapped workload: will you accept a periodic signed artifact upload (SFTP with FIPS TLS) or do you require physical media movement?
- Is the control plane allowed to see hashed metadata (non-PII) for billing/metrics, or must it be completely blind?

Attachments included: redwood-deploy-playbook-v1.pdf (high-level options: hosted/dedicated/private), ava-net-constraints.xlsx (you started filling this during the call), MAP-avahealth-20270809.docx (mutual action plan template).

If that matches what you heard, can you confirm ownership for item #3 and whether Ava wants Redwood to open a procurement SPOC with your vendor team?

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0118

From: Taylor Morgan <taylor.morgan@avahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: AvaHealth Security <security@avahealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 17:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data sovereignty playbook — post-call summary & MAP

Jonas — thanks for the concise summary, this is really helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Air-gap approach: for the initial PoC we prefer physical media for the audit archive (NDA-bound courier to a secure facility). For the production path we want an option that avoids frequent physical transport; can the playbook include both approaches?

2) Control plane telemetry: security policy allows the control plane to receive hashed request IDs and aggregate metrics only. No raw prompts or model outputs can traverse the public control plane.

3) NAT / egress whitelist: I’ll own item #3 and will coordinate with infra to populate ava-net-constraints.xlsx — I expect we can return a first pass by 2027-08-15.

4) KMS: we have an HSM provider (KeyForge) and can share their integration docs if Redwood can confirm compatibility with customer-managed KMS and HSM-backed key wrap.

On procurement: yes, please open a contact with procurement@avahealth.com — they need a draft SOW and an OLA for the air-gapped run.

Also looping in our security lead (security@avahealth.com) for any compliance-related items.

Quick note on latency: our triage UI p95 target is 120ms; if Redwood needs a small dedicated pool for that path, we’d like an estimate of committed throughput and cost.

Thanks — Taylor

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Morgan <taylor.morgan@avahealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data sovereignty playbook — post-call summary & MAP

Taylor — great notes. I’ll put together the KMS/HSM compatibility brief and include an outline of our HSM integration patterns (key wrapping vs. tenant-managed key material). Expect a short deck and a one-page checklist by Friday (2027-08-13).

On dedicated pool pricing: I’ll pull a two-tier estimate (committed and burst) that meets the 120ms p95 target for the triage workload — Jon, can you capture expected qps and typical prompt length for the estimate?

—Ben
Enterprise Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Morgan <taylor.morgan@avahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data sovereignty playbook — post-call summary & MAP

Thanks all — noted and filing the MAP in our shared Drive folder (link above). Two quick follow-ups: 

- Taylor: if you can drop the first-pass network rules into ava-net-constraints.xlsx by EOD 2027-08-15 that’s perfect. We’ll use that to validate the control-plane endpoints and confirm whether a private peering or VPC endpoint is required.
- Taylor / Ava security: for the air-gap PoC we’ll propose a runbook that supports both physical media ingestion and a signed SFTP artifact workflow; we’ll highlight tradeoffs and audit evidence paths.

I’ll schedule a short sync (30m) for next week to align on the procurement SOW and the draft cost estimate — propose Wed 2027-08-18 10:00am ET. Let me know if that works.

Jonas
